# Summary and Questions

# Experiment protocol

A 2D Rydberg array is driven across the (2+1)D Ising quantum phase transition to study collective dynamics of the ordered phase. The phase diagram of the square lattice is a square with the following regions:

![The phase diagram of the square lattice](/theory/Condensed_matter/TFIM/square-lattice_diag.png)

The experiment implement the time-depending Hamiltonian:
$$
H/\hbar = \Omega(t)/2 \sum_i \sigma_i^x - \sum_i n_i \Delta(t)  + \sum_{i<j} V_{ij} n_i n_j
$$

We can strictly define the local AF1 and AF2 phases: assume the lattice coordinates are $(x, y)$, and the atom state $n_{x,y} \in \{0, 1\}$ ($0$ represents the ground state $|g\rangle$, $1$ represents the excited state $|r\rangle$). 

- Perfect local AF1 phase: in the neighborhood of a site, the condition $n_{x,y} = 1$ is satisfied if and only if $x+y$ is even (i.e., all even sublattices are in $|r\rangle$, all odd sublattices are in $|g\rangle$). 
- Perfect local AF2 phase: in the neighborhood of a site, the condition $n_{x,y} = 1$ is satisfied if and only if $x+y$ is odd (i.e., all odd sublattices are in $|r\rangle$, all even sublattices are in $|g\rangle$).

![A global view of AF1 and AF2 phases](/Experiments/posts/1zone_archi/AF_phase.png)

:::{#lem-local-phase-order1 .callout-important icon="false"}
### (Local phase order post-processing)
The local phase order is calculated by the following formula:
$$
m_i = \frac{(-1)^{a+b}}{N_i} \sum_{\langle j, i \rangle} (n_i - n_j),
$$
where $i$ is a site index with $(x_i,y_i)$ coordinates, $N_i = 4$ is the number of nearest neighbors of site $i$, and $n_i$ is the Rydberg occupation number at site $i$.  Point $i$ is in AF1(AF2) phase iff $m_i = 1$ ($m_i = -1$).
:::

## An adiabatic preparation of AF1/AF2 phase

- Set up $R_b/a = 1.15$ ($a = 6.7~\mu\text{m}$ and  $\Omega = 2\pi \times 4.3~\text{MHz}$)
- Ramping on $\Omega$ while keeping $\Delta$ as a large negative fixed value. 
- While keeping $\Omega$ constant, ramping on $\Delta$ from a large negative value to a large positive value. 
  - The $\Delta(t)$ was obtained by optimizing the parameters $at^3 + bt^2 + ct + d$ to connecting 5 fixed points: initial detuning, final detuning, an inflection point where the slope reaches a minimum, and two additional points that define the duration of the slow part of the sweep.
- Ramping on $\Omega$ from a large value to a small value. Then measure the local phase order $m_i$ at each site $i$.
:::

![An adiabatic preparation of AF1/AF2 phase](Adiab.png)

Besides adiabtic preparision, they also tried the fast ramping protocol and analysis the KZM effect. A brief theoretical review of the KZM is given in [Here](/theory/Dynamics/KZM.qmd).
